newsitem.title: USA: "Excessive" rains damage North Dakota crops.
newsitem.headline: "Excessive" rains damage North Dakota crops.

text.p: Widespread thunderstorms dropped heavy rain acrss North Dakota during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.

"Excessive rains, particularly in the east, have caused problems with haying and weed control and raised concerns about crop diseases," the report said. "Standing water in fields caused significant damage to many crops, but especially in row crops such as dry edible beans, soybeans and potatoes."
Small grain development remained ahead of last year but mostly behind average.
The exception was spring wheat, which was 67 percent in the heading stage, ahead of 39 percent last week, 52 percent last year and 63 percent on average.

Spring wheat condition was rated 44 percent good to excellent, up from 41 percent at that level last week. Durum wheat was rated 28 percent good to excellent, against 27 percent at that level last week.

Late-season crops continued to grow at a pace slightly ahead of last year and average, with the exception of sugarbeets and potatoes, which were equal to average. Canola was also behind last year but the average was not available.
Potato and soybean condition dropped considerably while sugarbeet and dry edible bean condition also declined due to surplus soil moisture in major growing areas.
